title: Truss-based Why-not Community Search

problem.claim: Given a k-truss community and an excluded vertex, determine the minimum number of edges to insert so that the vertex joins the community.

contributions.claim: The truss-based why-not community search problem is NP-hard.
Two heuristic algorithms are proposed: an expansion-based algorithm and a simulation-based algorithm.
Optimizations are implemented to improve the efficiency of both algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world graphs are reported to demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of the methods and optimizations.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper introduces truss-based why-not community search and defines the edge-insertion objective.
The problem is characterized as NP-hard.
Two heuristic algorithms use incremental expansion or insertion followed by redundant-edge removal.
Additional optimizations are implemented for both algorithms.
Experiments on real-world graphs report efficiency and effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The task is formulated as minimizing edge insertions needed to include an excluded vertex in a k-truss community.

interpretation.claim: A why-not community task can be treated as a constrained graph-editing optimization problem.

application.claim: This formulation may support graph-based recommendation or transportation-planning applications.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the formulation is preferable to alternative community-search objectives.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proof of NP-hardness.
The abstract does not identify the real-world graphs, evaluation metrics, or comparative baselines.
The abstract does not provide quantitative experimental results.
